summary.text: John Boccieri is the Democratic candidate for Ohio House of Representatives District 58 in the November 3, 2026 general election, running against Republican Heather Fronk.
A former U.S. Air Force Reserve pilot, he previously served in the Ohio House of Representatives and the U.S. House of Representatives.

paragraphs.text: John Boccieri was born in Youngstown, Ohio, and lives in Poland, Ohio.
He earned a bachelor's degree in economics from Saint Bonaventure University in 1992 and a master's degree in business/public administration from Webster University in 1996.
Boccieri served in the U.S. Air Force from 1994 to 1998 and has been in the Air Force Reserve since 1998, where his career experience includes working as a squadron commander and evaluator pilot.
Boccieri began his career as a legislative aide to Ohio state representatives Greg DiDonato and Richard Cordray in 1992.
He served in the Ohio House of Representatives from 2001 to 2006 and represented Ohio's 16th Congressional District in the U.S. House from 2009 to 2011; Jim Renacci succeeded him in that seat.
He later returned to the Ohio House, representing District 59 until 2018, and in 2017 served on its Energy and Natural Resources, Insurance, and Public Utilities committees.
Boccieri was the Democratic nominee for Ohio State Senate District 33 in 2018, when Michael Rulli defeated him, 52.4 percent to 47.6 percent.
He advanced from the Democratic primary for District 58 on May 5, 2026.
